title: Doctoral Scholarship from the University of Innsbruck
program_type: Doctoral scholarship used as start-up, interim, bridge or final funding for doctoral candidates
duration: Maximum 24 months, with an interim review every 6 months; the 24-month period can be interrupted twice, each interruption not exceeding 6 months
description: The University of Innsbruck awards a doctoral scholarship as start-up, interim, bridge or final financing for doctoral candidates, with a monthly allowance of EUR 1,120 for a maximum of 24 months. Funding is granted in six-month blocks confirmed by an interim progress report from the dissertation supervisor, and the 24-month period can be interrupted twice, each interruption not exceeding six months. title: ISTA PhD Program (fully funded PhD employment)
official_source: Institute of Science and Technology Austria (ISTA)
program_type: Doctoral (PhD) programme funded through a salaried employment contract with the Institute
duration: All students receive 5-year employment contracts; students typically complete the programme in 4.5 to 6 years, can finish earlier in 4 or 4.5 years, or may ask for a one-year contract extension depending on the nature of the research.
description: ISTA states that PhD students are employed by the Institute and that all of them receive internationally competitive salaries and full social security coverage, with additional financial support to attend scientific conferences and workshops. ISTA charges no tuition fees and no application fee for its PhD, internship and scholarship programmes. Published gross salaries for 2026 range from EUR 3,053 to EUR 3,673 per month depending on whether the student holds a Bachelor's or Master's degree at admission, are paid 14 times a year, and rise once the Qualifying Exam is passed. title: Helmut Veith Stipend for Female Master's Students in Computer Science
program_type: Merit-based scholarship for female computer science master's students
duration: EUR 7000 per year; the stipend is annually awarded, with TU Wien reporting holders over up to two years
description: The Helmut Veith Stipend is an annually awarded grant for women pursuing a Master's programme in Computer Science at TU Wien taught in English, created in memory of Professor Helmut Veith (1971-2016). TU Wien states the benefits as "EUR 7000 per year" plus a "Waiver of tuition fees at TU Wien". The fund is set up by TU Wien, the Wolfgang Pauli Institute and the colleagues and friends of the late Prof. Veith. Applications are submitted electronically through the TU Wien job portal and are due by 30 November each year.

title: FWF ESPRIT (Early-Stage Program: Research - Innovation - Training)
program_type: Career development grant for early-career postdocs (principal investigator project)
description: ESPRIT (Early-Stage Program: Research - Innovation - Training) is an Austrian Science Fund career programme that lets highly qualified postdoc-level researchers lead an independent research project at an Austrian research institution. The FWF states a funding period of 36 months, paying the principal investigator's salary at the current senior postdoc rate plus project-specific costs of EUR 45,000 as a flat rate, or up to EUR 75,000 with justification. title: FWF ASTRA Awards
program_type: Career award for advanced postdocs (principal investigator project)
description: The FWF ASTRA Awards are a career funding programme launched in July 2024 for advanced postdocs in Austria who already have experience with independent research (R3 level). The FWF awards between EUR 500,000 and EUR 1 million per project over five years, plus an additional EUR 200,000 tenure package for female principal investigators who secure a permanent position within the first three years. The programme is decided by the FWF Scientific Board on the recommendation of an international jury following peer review and a hearing, with about 18 awards per call and half of them awarded to women.

title: Mannagetta Fellowships (Johann Wilhelm Ritter von Mannagetta Foundation at the Austrian Academy of Sciences)
official_source: Johann Wilhelm Ritter von Mannagetta Foundation (Austrian Academy of Sciences)
program_type: Completion fellowship for doctoral candidates in the humanities, social sciences, law and arts disciplines
description: The Mannagetta Fellowships are financed from the funds of the Johann Wilhelm Ritter von Mannagetta Foundation held at the Austrian Academy of Sciences and support doctoral candidates at Austrian universities in completing a doctoral thesis in the humanities, cultural and social sciences. Applicants must have started their doctoral studies at a university in Austria no more than three years before the submission deadline and need no more than another twelve months to finish.
